notes.title: From the Devs: Developing your Settlements
notes.notes:
[p]Hello again [i]Civ [/i]fans! Tom Shaw, Lead Producer at Firaxis Games, back again with another deep dive into some upcoming UI/UX improvements. In 1.2.2 we brought you the new and improved Loading Screen, [url="https://civilization.2k.com/civ-vii/from-the-devs/"][u]complete with an article outlining the what and why of it all[/u][/url]. With a more solid technical foundation in place, we're now ready to focus on gameplay and deliver more impactful UI improvements. Today, we’re giving you an early look at some changes to help with expanding and growing your empire! [/p][p][/p][p]Specifically, we’re highlighting changes to improve your experience at these decision points:[/p][olist][*][p]What should I build?[/p][/*][*][p]Where do I place constructibles? [/p][/*][*][p]Should I go for an Improvement or Specialist? 
[/p][/*][/olist][p]Choices like these are critical to the long-term success of your campaign, so having access to the information you need when making these decisions is paramount. Without this, it can be all too easy to fall into states of analysis paralysis or, even worse, indifference. Our goal is for you to always feel informed and empowered in these moments and we recognize there’s plenty of room for improvement in reaching that. [/p][p][/p][p]So, without further ado, here’s a sneak peak at what we’ve been working on and why…[/p][p][/p][h2]The Production Menu[/h2][h3][i]What should I build?[/i][/h3][p][/p][p]The settlement production menu is arguably one of, if not [i]the[/i], most important UI elements in a Civ game. The choices made here are fundamental to building your empire’s engine, pursuing campaign-specific goals, and ultimately dominating your enemies.
[/p][p]Our current version displays a predictive yield presentation on Buildings, Wonders, and Unique Improvements intended to help players make these decisions.[b] [/b]Unfortunately, we’ve learned that the presentation of these yields is often confusing for players, as it doesn’t present all of the data needed to make an informed decision. These yields can also contribute to a lack of engagement with critical decision points by encouraging the player to simply choose the biggest number; making this moment feel more like an Idle Clicker than Grand Strategy. I admit I’ve been guilty of this myself. [/p][p][/p][p][b]The main problem with this presentation, and what we’re addressing with this update, is that these yields are acting as a recommender without actually being one.[/b] The yields presented are supposed to show the highest possible yield currently available. This sounds great in theory, but remember earlier when I said they might not have all the data you need? This is due to the sheer depth of the game. There are so many factors that can modify the yield output of a given tile. These modifiers can come from many sources, like your Leader Abilities (permanent), Social Policies (temporary), and Building Adjacencies (contextual). These can be modified further with Leader Attributes and Wonders. Additionally, Specialists create their own issue where they're usually modifying these yields for some, but not all, of the Building options in the menu. All this creates a data management headache of needing to access and communicate to the player “Everything, Everywhere, All at Once” which is an outstanding movie, but a terrible approach to making responsive data calls.
[/p][p]Ultimately the potential yields are being overly emphasized in this context given their value and accuracy, so we moved their display to the actual placement decision context. [b]But without the potential yields, how will I know what to build?[/b][/p][p][/p][p]In addition to basic information like name, build time, and advisor recommendations, the production menu now presents a constructible's base yields along with one or both of these, if applicable:
[/p][list][*][p][b]Warehouse Improvements: [/b]The current number of Improvements, in this Settlement, that will benefit from a given warehouse effect. [/p][/*][*][p][b]Highest Adjacency Tile: [/b]The most Adjacencies this building currently has available in the Settlement.[/p][p][/p][/*][/list][p]We’ve found these additions to be very useful at highlighting potential opportunities [i]before[/i] diving into the building placement context. No more manually counting Improvements to see which Warehouse(s) you should prioritize or avoid building! Plus, when you’ve got an opportunity to cash in on a large number of Adjacencies this number really helps call that out.
[/p][p]One of the great things about working on [i]Civilization[/i] is that the audience is so large and varied, but that also presents a challenge: which information should we display? For example, is it better to count all the Adjacencies, since they're all a bonus you'll get, or only count the ones specific to the base Building's bonus? What if that changes due to a Wonder or Leader Attribute? We've erred on the side of a simple, clear calculation that we believe serves the widest audience, but we'd love to hear your thoughts on this or other changes we've made.
[/p][p]We’ve also given our Building, Improvement, and Wonder tooltips a much-needed overhaul to improve clarity and readability. The previous formatting, or lack of, made it easy for important information to get lost, leading many players to skip over these details entirely. As a result, the strategic impact of certain choices wasn’t always clear.
[/p][p]To help players better understand the effects of their decisions, we’ve restructured the layout and presentation of these tooltips. Cleaner, consistent, formatting and organization should make the information easier to absorb at a glance.[/p][p][/p][p]Check out the before-and-after comparison below to see the difference for yourself:[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45050851/fc7ebb9606ebaa52e3624ec1b6b677a8f899449f.jpg"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45050851/f6e220fc87c7a76fb0bab8accb7dad50f3418db3.jpg"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]Beyond the formatting improvements (yay, bulleted lists are here!), you’ll also notice some new content: Tags. These offer a quick, high-level summary of what a constructible (Building, Wonder, or Unique Improvement) is, or key elements associated with it, helping you grasp its role and relevance at a glance.
[/p][p]Another opportunity we identified is the inconsistent visibility of yield losses, such as those caused by maintenance or overbuilding. We’re fixing that. In an effort to help players clearly see the full impact of their choices and understand the strategic tradeoffs, [b]we will now be showing yield losses in all of the contexts discussed in this article[/b].[/p][p]We recognize this is a big change, but it’s one the team is genuinely excited about. We really believe it’s a better experience; not just for players now, but for the long-term health of the game. That said, if you give it a shot and find it’s not for you, no worries, [b]we’ve kept the original presentation* as an option.[/b] [/p][p][i]*With one exception, this presentation will now also include the negative yields as mentioned above.[/i][/p][p][/p][h2]Building Placement[/h2][h3][i]I picked something to build, now where do I place it?[/i][/h3][p][/p][p]Placing a Building might seem simple on the surface, but it’s often anything but. You’re weighing a number of factors, including the Building’s Base Yields, tile stats, Adjacencies, Specialists, Overbuilding, District connections, unique Civ or Leader abilities, your long-term strategy, and so on. If you're the kind of player who loves optimizing every one of these choices (hi, fellow Builder-type here), this can be incredibly satisfying. What’s less satisfying? Doing all that math with minimal help from the UI. So, we’ve made some improvements.
[/p][p]Here’s what you’ll see right away:[/p][list][*][p]New yield indicators (green and red up/down arrows) that more clearly show gains and losses at a glance.[/p][/*][*][p]A revamped building slot icon, replacing the old blue dot with something far more legible.[/p][/*][*][p]Green yield numbers on tiles with the highest net yields or highest primary yield to highlight some tiles for consideration.[/p][p][/p][/*][/list][p][i]*This isn’t a recommendation or ‘best move’ hint, it's simply data. What you do with it is up to you. I’m not taking the blame for your misplaced Garden. ;) [/i][/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45050851/63e64dbd7a70f1e6738fd81cf695f642b938e19a.jpg"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45050851/e8ff89fd5bb233d3afce6af8496cbd106b15c4b5.jpg"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]Once you start playing with it, you’ll notice:[/p][list][*][p]The left panel dynamically updates when you hover a valid tile, showing a summary of changes to Settlement yields, Overbuilding effects, and any changes to the tile type.[/p][/*][*][p]New arrow visuals for Adjacency clearly showing what yield types you're gaining and from where.[/p][/*][*][p]The cursor now reinforces your action, switching to the “place me here” arrow when hovering a valid tile.[/p][/*][*][p]An optional expanded view in the left panel for players like me who want the full breakdown: before and after stats, deltas, adjacencies, etc. neatly itemized.[/p][p][/p][/*][/list][p][i]*For now the labeling for why you’re getting an adjacency is limited, but we intend to have the detailed view get very thorough, informing you of the specific reason why you’re getting an adjacency, such as Machu Picchu or a given social policy.[/i][/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45050851/e7a4728a2bce7c2dedf9b44d346579b8b1bb5bae.jpg"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45050851/c6a0735b88884912b7aebcd82907ff1527da5449.jpg"][/img][/p][p]We still won’t tell you exactly where to place your building. That decision, and all the clever planning behind it, remains yours. But with these UI enhancements, we hope it feels less like guesswork and more like what it should be: a strategic, informed choice that plays to your strengths.[/p][p][/p][h2]Growth Events[/h2][h3][i]What’s better: Improvements or Specialists?[/i]
[/h3][p]Classic [i]Civilization [/i]answer: it depends. 
[/p][p]And like many decisions in [i]Civ VII[/i], the answer hinges on a lot: tile yields, Resources, Adjacency potential, maintenance costs, Specialist slots, border expansion, future plans, and more. So, we’ve upgraded how that decision is presented to help you make more informed choices without needing to guess.
[/p][p]Growth Events now share the same visual language and structure as the new Building Placement screen. That means more clarity, more consistency, and a smoother decision-making experience. 
[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45050851/2a94db829edbe41aa044d3667a6d63439e90e0f5.jpg"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45050851/2077e09c2a8c7915122c0d4aa9fbe28355f9eb86.jpg"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45050851/6a3945506543cf7242c3b6788b04d469e9ea8850.jpg"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45050851/4c2dbbee0b31c4716fbe985d591da7abfd5d7fb7.jpg"][/img][/p][p]Here’s what you’ll see when your settlement grows:[/p][list][*][p]The Growth Event panel on the left clearly lays out your two options: Add Improvement or Add Specialist. Except in the case where you haven’t unlocked Specialists, this comes online from that point forward. [/p][list][*][p]Each option includes a clearer explanation of what it does and how it works.[/p][p][/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][p]When you start comparing tiles, all the same tools from Building Placement are at your disposal:[/p][list][*][p]Settlement yield change previews, updated in real-time as you explore your options.[/p][/*][*][p]Clearer breakdowns of adjacency bonuses, maintenance costs, and tile types.[/p][/*][*][p]A full before-and-after view, so you know exactly what you’re gaining (or giving up) with each choice.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p]We’ve also refined how Specialists are presented. Urban tiles now display their current and max capacity more clearly, making it easier to see where you’re under-utilized or already full.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45050851/df53e6ea461dab8e51b93c1abebeca4856f4584e.jpg"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45050851/ec8d1eab842b226983c51ca0fdcbc51349a276ee.jpg"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45050851/ac16efdc4dd0b0ea4bfb0f9c8e849ea197af5eef.jpg"][/img][/p][p]Just like with Building Placement, we’re not here to make the call for you; but we [i]are[/i] making sure you’ve got the information you need to make the right one for [i]your[/i] strategy.[/p][p][/p][h2]Cool, but when?[/h2][p]I’m happy to share that these changes will be coming soon with our 1.2.5 update. But we’re still not done. There’s more to do in this space and push these experiences even further. In addition to continued iteration here, the team is hard at work improving the presentation and usability of the Settlement Banners, Overbuilding experience, and a whole new Commerce hub. 
[/p][p]We look forward to hearing how you are experiencing this new update, so please keep sharing your feedback. We’re excited about these changes and we hope you are too. Stay tuned for more UI/UX updates. Until then, Stay Civilized![/p][p][/p][p][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/1295660/Sid_Meiers_Civilization_VII/"][/dynamiclink][/p]

notes.title: Civilization 7 dev explains how the revamped 4X map generator bolts together continents from Voronoi diagrams
notes.notes:
Firaxis and 2K Games are working on a Civilization 7 update that revamps the game's map generation, while adding a couple of city states and rounding out Napoleon's skillset. It's slated to land sometime in the week of September 29th. Why am I writing about it right now? Because senior graphics engineer Ken Pruiksma has just posted a little blog about the intricacies of strategy game map generation that caused Beethoven's Ode To Joy to play tinnily in my head.

This is almost certainly a reflection of emotional diarrhea brought on by minor insomnia brought on by a nagging foot injury. Still, there's something... uplifting about the motions of plate tectonics as approximated by computer code. Perhaps you, kind stranger, will be similarly moved.

Read more

notes.title: From the Devs: Improved Map Generation
notes.notes: [p]Hello [i]Civ[/i] fans! Ken Pruiksma, Senior Graphics Engineer at Firaxis Games, here to share some behind-the-scenes updates on map generation.[/p][p][/p][p]When [i]Civilization VII [/i]first shipped, the map generation technique we used focused on ensuring balanced play while following some new gameplay rules around things like Deep Ocean and Distant Lands. This technique, which has its roots in previous [i]Civ[/i] games, created fair maps, but also made them predictable. This caused the exploration phase of the game to be potentially  less rewarding (which isa problem when the first X in 4X is Explore!) We heard from you that maps felt too repetitive, and we agreed.  [/p][p][/p][p]Something else we heard loud and clear from the community is that the straight-edged coastlines that could occur between the two major halves was hindering the play experience. Part of the fantasy of Civ is that you’re playing an alternative history of Earth, and when the maps don’t feel plausibly Earth-like, it detracts from the experience (outside some exceptions like perfectly balanced multiplayer where you’re opting into a mirrored game).[/p][p][/p][p]So, we’ve made some big updates with 1.2.5. We wanted map generation that felt more natural and less repetitive, while still keeping balance in mind where it matters. Out of that work came two brand new map types to choose from: [b]Continents and Islands [/b](two large continents, with islands) and [b]Pangea and Islands [/b](one large continent, with islands). Both are built on an entirely new technique: [b]Voronoi map generation.[/b][/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45050851/6d23379c2120c8a7d855f672fe688864dbc70eed.jpg"][/img][/p][p][/p][h2]Voronoi Maps[/h2][p]I’m a graphics engineer, which means I spend most of my time making beautiful pixels, but I’ve always had a soft spot for procedural generation and the algorithms that drive it. When the chance came up to help the gameplay team with map generation, I couldn’t resist.[/p][p][/p][p]I had an idea about using Voronoi diagrams to dynamically grow landmasses using some rules. After throwing a quick test together, the idea showed promise.[/p][p][/p][p]Without getting too technical, the Voronoi technique completely changes how we approach map generation. Previously, fractal noise had been used to create maps, and it works really well when it can be applied uniformly to the whole map. However it can be hard to steer towards specific gameplay needs. Voronoi diagrams, on the other hand, give us structure we can build rules on top of, so maps can stay organic while still meeting the gameplay requirements of Civ VII. [/p][p][/p][p]Let’s walk through how this works.[/p][olist][*][p]Randomly spray a bunch of points onto the map. The more points we spray, the higher the resolution. We’ll start low res.[/p][/*][*][p]Draw lines around each point dividing them into “cells”. You end up with something that looks a bit like cracked glass.[/p][/*][*][p]Select some starting cells. These are the seeds of tectonic plates in the game map, similar to the tectonic plates that form our Earth.[/p][/*][*][p]Each plate grows, one cell at a time, following some configurable rules, until the whole map is filled.  Each plate gets a rotation and movement direction. This is your map’s crust, and will be used to help influence the growth of continents later.[/p][/*][*][p]Now spray many more dots for a higher resolution version! Draw those lines again to get another shattered glass look sitting on top of your tectonic plates.[/p][/*][*][p]Choose some new starting points for the primary landmasses, and grow them once again following a custom set of configurable rules. These rules can do things like influence landmasses to grow along plate boundaries (especially if they’re colliding), avoid the poles, and prefer certain latitudes, just to name a few. This is also where we can apply gameplay-based restrictions, like ensuring Homelands and Distant Lands are separated by a Deep Ocean.[/p][/*][*][p]Based on the map’s settings, we then grow islands, erode the coastline, add mountains and volcanoes, and perform other finishing touches. Many of these steps involve the same set of generic rules used earlier to determine where features are placed.[/p][/*][*][p]Once finished, we overlay the hex grid and then hand the map off to the gameplay layer to determine tile types, yields, resources, starting location, and more. [/p][/*][/olist][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45050851/624f91fd98a39cb8ce2eabb6755085bb60eb7060.gif"][/img][/p][p]The result is that the maps are far more varied and look much more natural. Things that were impossible before can now appear regularly. For example, Homelands and Distant Lands might be North and South of each other. Continents may share a large border, be connected by a small isthmus, or be separated by a sea. There may be a chain of islands between Homelands and Distant Lands – or maybe there won’t! The islands could all be clustered in a corner or scattered around, and they’re even allowed to merge, possibly causing a continent-sized super-island![/p][p][/p][p]One thing to keep in mind is that we intentionally tuned the settings to generate “normal” maps (i.e. natural-feeling maps with standard gameplay) about 95% of the time. This means, there is a small chance for super weird layouts. Part of the fun of Civ is sometimes landing on a bizarre start or weird map thanks to the RNG gods. If you land on an odd map, please share those![/p][p][/p][p]Most importantly, this all means that while you’re exploring your starting location and surrounding area, you can’t make any assumptions about the shape of the world. When playing on these new maps, I've felt the mystery and excitement again as I explore in the early game and have no idea what’s going to appear in the next hex![/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45050851/8a6fb04cede759597ce48a35f74edba4b7a08b31.gif"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45050851/8a275fdc8a158095f5812eeae62368bb1f7453d7.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][h2]Just the Beginning[/h2][p]With the release of 1.2.5, you’ll find new maps named “Continents and Islands” and “Pangea and Islands” that use this new approach, with the first being the new default in singleplayer games If you’d like to play with the old maps, they are still there under their original names. These older maps may be preferred in a multiplayer setting where the lower variance helps keep the balance among players.  [/p][p][/p][p]This is just the beginning for our revamped work on maps! This technique was built with customization, expansion, and modding in mind from the beginning. As a result, you can expect more map options, future improvements to existing map types, and more exposed settings over time as we continue to develop this system. And yes, modders, Voronoi maps are available to you, too! You’ll find the scripts and configuration settings used to generate them within the game files along with the specific settings we used for our official maps. We’d love to see how you use this new approach to make new map types. [/p][p][/p][p]Finally, we’d love to see the maps you’re all getting, so please keep posting them on social media or in the official [url="https://discord.com/invite/civilizationofficial"]Civ Discord[/url]. We’re excited about these changes and we hope you are too. Stay tuned for more map updates. Until then, have fun exploring![/p]

notes.title: This Month in Civ: August Update, News Recap, and More
notes.notes:
[h1][b]Welcome Back![/b][/h1][p]Hey,[i] Civ [/i]fans! Welcome to This Month in [i]Civ[/i]! August has been a busy month, and we’re kicking things off with a recap of everything that’s happened so far. [/p][p]Let’s dive in! [/p][h3][b]Update 1.2.4[/b][/h3][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45050851/7dc91864f35b9988cf88e9d032fb2eb026c30b7e.png"][/img][/p][h3][b]Update 1.2.4 & Patch 1 are here![/b][/h3][p]This update adds a few improvements to the “Continuity” setting by increasing the maximum Gold and Influence retained, while keeping your alliances intact when you enter a new Age. We’re shaking up empires with an exciting rebalance to Wonders, with some minor Yield tweaks alongside bigger changes that enhance their power. These changes open up possibilities to explore new strategies and breathe new life into old favorites. Rounding out the gameplay section, we’ve added a few quality-of-life changes like edge panning and some improvements to controller support to smooth out empire management.[/p][p]Discover the full details[url="https://civilization.2k.com/civ-vii/game-update-notes/"] [u]here[/u][/url], or join Game Designer Carl Harrison in our newest Developer Update Video as he dives into the details below. [/p][previewyoutube="mRNnvnP-3bQ;full"][/previewyoutube][p]Also, Update 1.2.4 - Patch 1 is out now to players on Steam and Epic! This patch improves game setup, quality-of-life features, and addresses a few bugs.  Read the full patch notes [url="https://civilization.2k.com/civ-vii/game-update-notes/"]here[/url], and also a message from our creative director, Ed Beach.[/p][p][/p][h3][b]Plushies have landed![/b][/h3][p][b]War Elephant Plushie[/b][/p][p]Pre-orders are open for your first ally in every game of [i]Civilization VII[/i], as The War Elephant plushie always has your back. Inspired by the Maurya India Unique Unit, the Purabhettarah, this plushie is ready to guide you through fierce battles, or can be the perfect gift to begin an alliance. For a tusked desktop pal, look no further, as this historic companion has you covered. Pre-orders are open for a limited time, so snag one while you can [u][url="https://youtooz.com/products/war-elephant-plush-9-inch"]here[/url][/u]. [/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45050851/e2d738b1e573105088ccd13cf7735490df0e8713.png"][/img][/p][h3][b]Benjamin and Confucius Plushies[/b][/h3][p]That's right - the War Elephant isn't marching alone! Benjamin Franklin and Confucius are following close behind. Sweep aside the pens and bills to squeeze them in, as our friends at Makeship have made the great leaders pocket-sized. These are just the first few historic icons of the lineup, so get ready for more surprises down the road. Get yours [u][url="https://www.makeship.com/shop/creator/civilization-vii"]here[/url][/u].[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45050851/6eca2f6efb897ba54648ac33326ac0a0a9dfaa06.png"][/img][/p][h3][b]HyperX + Civilization Merch Drop[/b][/h3][p]The HyperX + [i]Civilization [/i]alliance is finally ready to share the secret blueprints to help you achieve a Culture Victory. The partnership has brought the best of Science and Culture together, bringing you [i]Civ[/i]-themed HyperX headphone covers and Wonder-themed key caps. Whether you're looking to add a splash of color to your headset or raise the bar with Wonders for your RGB spectacle, we've got you covered. Check out the content [u][url="https://hyperx.com/blogs/hyperx-blog/civilization-vii"]here[/url][/u]! [/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45050851/23beacbd3302c4e24d3338c477e40e2fa47bfaae.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][h1][b]Community[/b][/h1][h3][b]The Devs Talk Llamas[/b][/h3][p]We've been watching the chatter around the [i]Civ[/i] community about the Llama resource. "Why are they in the game?" "Why do they give happiness and production?" And of course, "Why are they so cute?” We're tagging in Taymoor from the Game Design team to reveal the inspiration behind the addition of Llamas. [/p][p][/p][h3][b]Firaxis Game Designer, Taymoor, says…[/b][/h3][p]"When we're looking for Resources to add into the game, there are a lot of things to take into account. In the 1.2.0 update to Resources, the biggest factors were biome, mechanical effect, and how well we were representing various natural resources from around the world. Llamas were suggested early and made everyone smile every time we talked about them, so they had to go in. We figured they'd be a hit with our audience too (the internet loves llamas!). Given their use as pack animals in South America, we knew some of their effects had to be production-based, but with how much joy we had in bringing them to the game, their main effect ended up focusing on Happiness." [/p][p][img src="data:image/png;base64,"][/img][/p][h3][b]Player Spotlight[/b][/h3][p][b]Jordi Taeka[/b][/p][p][b]“Day 103 - The Face of the Future (and Past)”[/b][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45050851/258f34b93d9521fb60b61c41bf0619cf7302f144.png"][/img][/p][p][b]Shiningeek [/b][/p][p][b]“Isabella players only want one thing, and it's disgusting.”[/b][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45050851/0ea2a070d5a9c014f22f60441a679751e04a8745.png"][/img][/p][h3][b]We'll see you here next month![/b][/h3][p]News aside, thank you for all your feedback, both critical and kind. We know your passion for [i]Civilization [/i]drives your comments, and you want to see the best game possible. Please keep voicing your thoughts and contributing to a [i]Civilization[/i] you believe in.  If you haven't added your voice, start in our[url="https://discord.com/invite/civilizationofficial"] [u]Official Discord[/u][/url] and give feedback or chat with others about the updates. The Steam discussions are also a place to talk about feature requests, suggestions, guides, mods, and more. Stay connected with [i]Civ[/i] news delivered straight to your inbox. [u][url="https://civilization.2k.com/civ-vii/2k-account-benefits/#newsletter"]Sign up[/url][/u] for our newsletter now—your empire will thank you.
[/p]

notes.title: Civilization 7 is testing a "harsher" option for its divisive Age Transitions
notes.notes:
The transitions between the three major ages of a Civilization 7 match have been a hot topic ever since release. Arguably the biggest shake-up to the 4X series' formula in the new entry, the decision to pick a new civ at the start of each era has been divisive. In order to give Civ 7 players more flexibility and appease those wanting a more classic experience, Firaxis recently introduced Age Transition Impact settings - Regroup is for those that enjoy the new approach, and Continuity for those that want to carry more over to each age and keep things more stable. Well, a third, "harsher" option is now being considered, and it's called Collapse.

Read the rest of the story...

notes.title: Update 1.2.4 - Patch 1 - Aug 27, 2025
notes.notes:
[p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45050851/7d3e9c7b986bcee7909424a1c0a23031ac51c07a.png"][/img][/p][p]Update 1.2.4 - Patch 1 is rolling out now to players on Steam and Epic! This patch improves game setup and quality-of-life features, making Age Transitions and other game settings easier to manage across campaigns, and addresses several player-reported issues. This patch will be coming to additional platforms with the next [i]Civilization VII[/i] update.

[b]Before we get to the changes, a message from Ed Beach, Creative Director:[/b]
[/p][p]Over the past two updates, we've introduced some new optionality for how players approach Age Transitions. We appreciate the community's feedback to this new optionality, and I wanted to quickly outline some upcoming iteration that we've been working on.
[/p][p]First, a quick recap: In Update 1.2.3 we introduced the [b]Age Transition Impact[/b] setting, allowing users to select either [b]Regroup [/b](where Age Transitions behave as originally designed) or [b]Continuity [/b](which retains the map locations of all your units). Several additional changes to soften the Age Transition if you selected Continuity mode have also shipped within 1.2.3 and 1.2.4.[/p][p][/p][p]Continuity Mode is a nice way to allow players less disruption to their military campaigns if they like to be fighting continuously from one Age to the next. I don’t use that setting often in my games, but I did enjoy it recently when I played a full campaign with Genghis Khan as my leader.[/p][p][/p][p]When we introduced the Age Transition Impact setting, however, we made it an Advanced Setup option, so it wasn't something every player looked at when starting a new Civ VII campaign. And because Continuity Mode became the new default, players who prefer the Regroup experience would have to remember to select this advanced setting before each new game. Introducing that friction was not our intent.[/p][p][/p][p]To that end, we have prioritized a new feature where some of our main Game Settings are now "sticky" (so Civ VII will remember the setting from your previous game). Age Transition Impact, Game Speed, and Difficulty are the first three settings we are going to make sticky like this, and they will all be primary Game Settings that you see before you launch any new game. Now I can set it to Regroup and leave it there – unless I have plans for a particularly conquest-heavy campaign, like my one with Genghis.
[/p][p]Finally, we want to let our community know that we do have ideas for a third Age Transition Impact setting, something on the other, harsher side of Regroup, a setting we are tentatively calling Collapse. It’s still early in testing, and we’ll need time to see if it feels fun and fits well into the game. If it does, we’ll look into when it might make sense to include it in a future update. We’ll have more to share once it’s further along![/p][p][/p][p]We know Ages have sparked both excitement and debate across the Civilization community. We appreciate the community's ongoing feedback as this system continues to evolve, and look forward to delivering additional enhancements in the coming months. Thank you for the ongoing support.[/p][p][/p][p]Stay Civilized![/p][p]
[/p][h1][b]Patch Notes[/b][/h1][list][*][p]Made several improvements to game setup, including:[/p][list][*][p]Moved the [b]Age Transition[/b] setting out of Advanced Options for easier access.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Age Transition Impact, Game Speed,[/b] and [b]Difficulty[/b] are now sticky; the game will remember these settings between Create Game sessions after starting a game.[/p][list][*][p][b]Dev Note:[/b] No more restarting because you forgot to change your difficulty again![/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Difficulty Advanced Options settings are always visible & dynamically update to Custom when you change individual settings.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Addressed a reported issue that prevented mouse clicks from registering as expected.[/p][/*][*][p]The debug menu can now be accessed in single-player when debug panels are enabled and the keybind is used.[/p][/*][*][p]Addressed a reported issue that could occur when loading crossplay saves.[/p][/*][*][p]Addressed a reported issue when repeatedly opening and closing the Resource Screen.[/p][/*][*][p]Addressed a reported issue where Deluxe Cosmetics were not properly granted to players on the Epic Games Store.[/p][/*][/list][p]
If you’re still running into issues after this patch, please let us know through our [url="https://civilization.2k.com/civ-vii/game-update-notes/#:~:text=If%20you%E2%80%99re%20still%20running%20into%20issues%20after%20this%20patch%2C%20please%20let%20us%20know%20through%20our%20support%20portal.%C2%A0"][u]support portal[/u][/url].[/p]

notes.title: Update 1.2.4 – Aug 19, 2025
notes.notes:
[p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45050851/299f97276dfdf8a6d762848c5251a76ae713d563.png"][/img][/p][p]Update 1.2.4 is rolling out now! As we work toward some larger changes and new features, this update focuses on steady improvements: further improving Age Transitions, rebalancing Wonders, adding more quality-of-life touches, and tidying things up with a round of addressed issues. 
[/p][p]A few quick notes before you dive in:
[/p][list][*][p]While we aim to maintain backwards compatibility for existing saves as much as possible, some new abilities or effects may not appear until you start a new game or advance to the next Age in your current campaign. For the best experience, we recommend starting a new game, or continuing your current game into the next Age.[/p][/*][*][p]If you encounter any new issues, try disabling any mods, as some may not yet be compatible with the latest update.[/p][/*][*][p]Are you playing on Steam and want to finish your current save under a previous version? You can do so using our legacy Steam beta branch.[/p][/*][/list][p]
Read on for the full notes below![/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45050851/bc8fba950b0b49e166e287bce97b51a534ed0ede.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][h1][b]Wonder Balance[/b][/h1][p][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXfHRsE8j-U6Gu7wNGpW-c5PMt2nuK3V5Pg2hbSjnoyShtmrSoquX0us8aX5_xb32cCVuqzLx8EgobUqqRvoRPw7LlmXxMG8qwJ6SGT4Cq_cAKj84iM8UZ1IJQN4bNzYYRsv-aAaEQ?key=YizRxL45zWAXlPgf2riVXw"][/img][/p][p]Wonders have always been a topic of fond discussion in the community. We love seeing your Wonder Tier Lists, and debating the merits of each Wonder's ability against their unlock and placement conditions. These make it fun for us to approach Wonder rebalancing, and to try to address the points made by the fans![/p][p]In Update 1.2.4, we've made a major round of adjustments to Wonders in every Age. We've moved the unlock location for Wonders around for better timing, like Erdene Zuu being available earlier, or to avoid overlapping, like separating Colossus and Monks Mound from being on the same Civic branch. We've expanded placement conditions, like relaxing the Desert restriction for the Pyramids and adding Grassland Mountains to Machu Pikchu.[/p][p]When a Wonder is a clear must-pick every game, it's time for a nerf, so we've reduced the strength of Gate of All Nations and House of Wisdom. But we've also buffed the effects of many, many Wonders to make them feel better and bring them into a more playable space. Check out the Wonders that enhance terrain like Petra – we've addressed the fact that building over the enhanced terrain removes the Wonder's effect![/p][p]The full list of Wonder changes are included in the notes below!

[/p][h1][b]Gameplay[/b][/h1][p][/p][h2]Advisors[/h2][list][*][p](★ – Community Influenced Item) Made several improvements to Advisor Warnings, including:[/p][list][*][p]"Trailing in Technology" and "Trailing in Civics" warnings no longer occur at Difficulty Levels of Sovereign and above.[/p][/*][*][p]Made updates to "Competing Wonder" warning, including:[/p][list][*][p]Warning now appears in all Ages (not just Antiquity).[/p][/*][*][p]Clicking "Take Me There" moves you to the other player's copy of the Wonder if possible.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Added new Advisor Warning: "Codex with a potential home but not assigned one." This is a variant of the existing warning "Codex with no Home."[/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][p]
[/p][h2]Age Transition Improvements[/h2][list][*][p](★) Alliances are now kept on Age Transition when playing on the Continuity setting.[/p][/*][*][p](★) More Gold/Influence is now carried over when playing on the Continuity setting.[/p][list][*][p][b]Dev note: [/b]We are aware of balance concerns around the Continuity setting and are looking into changes across the game that can be made to help smooth out the experience for players.
[/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][h2]AI[/h2][list][*][p]Trade with AI no longer fails due to assigning a Resource it thought it could.[/p][/*][*][p]AI now focuses more on transitioning Independents into City-States.[/p][/*][*][p]AI now has more reasonable logic in the Peace Deal menu.[/p][/*][*][p]Higher Difficulty AI no longer builds a functional duplicate wall on the same tile when the AI captures another Settlement.[/p][/*][*][p]AI leaders no longer accept an alliance if they will have to break it immediately, such as being at war with one of their allies.[/p][/*][*][p]Independent Power AI no longer fails to move their Units until provoked.[/p][/*][*][p]AI players now aggressively pursue final Victory Projects and Wonders after completing Legacy Paths.[/p][/*][*][p]AI will now properly favor Coastal tiles when available when navigating the Ocean to avoid ship damage.[/p][p][/p][/*][/list][h2]Age Transition[/h2][list][*][p]Spain is now properly unlocked with Lafayette when transitioning to the Exploration Age.[/p][/*][*][p]Mongolia is now properly unlocked after Age Transition when playing as one of Mongolia's recommended Leaders.[/p][/*][*][p]\[Right to Rule DLC] During Advanced Start, Genghis Khan no longer receives policies from the Han and Ming civs as they are not recommended civilizations.[/p][p][/p][/*][/list][h2]Camera Improvements[/h2][list][*][p](★) Added an edge-panning option for platforms with mouse input.[/p][list][*][p][b]Dev note[/b]: We heard those of you who prefer edge-panning instead of click-drag or keyboard map navigation, so we brought it back. [/p][h1][b]Narrative[/b][/h1][list][*][p]Addressed reported issues preventing certain events from triggering.[/p][/*][*][p]Corrected various tutorial text and icon issues in Narrative Events.[/p][/*][*][p]Updated the description of Investigation Discoveries in the Civilopedia entry for Discoveries.[/p][/*][*][p]Events that have Yield costs now clarify that they may cause their civ to have negative Yield gains due to penalties, maintenance, and other costs.[/p][/*][*][p]Addressed a reported issue where the Narrative Event UI could pop up without prompting the button to display one.[/p][/*][*][p][b]The Artilleryman[/b]: The reward tooltip now properly reflects the reward gained.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Ashes[/b]:[b] [/b]Rewards are changed to one granting Culture and the other Gold.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Bodhisattva[/b]: Event can now correctly be completed.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Doctor's Orders[/b]: The Healing bonus reward now applies in Friendly Territory.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Echoes of History[/b]: The reward tooltip for the second option now awards a Production bonus towards training Explorers.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Form and Formlessness[/b]: The reward tooltip now correctly says, "+1 Policy Slot."[/p][/*][*][p][b]If Needs Be[/b]: Quest can now be completed correctly.[/p][/*][*][p][b]The Invisible World[/b]: This event will now only trigger for Chola or Majapahit. Additionally the second option in this event now displays the correct text.[/p][/*][*][p][b]An Invitation to War[/b]: Clarified text on the Options' Reward tooltips.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Obstinacy[/b]: The icon for the Yield cost on the first option is now displayed for this event.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Rise of the Burghers[/b]: Event now has a second reward option.[/p][/*][*][p][b]A Royal Procession: [/b]Event can now be completed with unique Units that replace the Slinger Unit.[/p][/*][*][p][b]A Sheaf of Arrows[/b]: The second option now awards "+2 Happiness on Armorer."[/p][/*][*][p][b]Tiers of the Hunt[/b]: Rewards only apply to the Palace now.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Wasted Breath[/b]: Quest progress is now displayed correctly.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Waves of Gold[/b]: Event now refers to Treasure Convoy Units instead of Treasure Fleet Units.[/p][/*][*][p][b]The Way Things Are[/b]: Clarified the description on the reward tooltip for the second option.[/p][p][/p][/*][/list][h1][b]Audio[/b][/h1][list][*][p]Addressed various audio localization issues across the game.[/p][/*][*][p]Made various quality-of-life improvements across leader and narrator voice-over.[/p][/*][*][p]Made various quality-of-life improvements across UI.[/p][/*][*][p]Added SFX to Narrative Rewards, Capture Settlement, and Raze or Keep Settlement. [/p][/*][*][p]Notification sound added when another player completes a milestone.[/p][/*][*][p]Addressed various reported audio issues.

notes.title: Take-Two boss says Civilization 7 projections 'are very consistent with our initial expectations' despite its rough start: 'The key thing is that Civ has always been a slow burn'
notes.notes: Civilization 7 got off to a rough start when it dropped earlier this year: Systemic changes, particularly the addition of "ages," proved deeply divisive, but there was also a slew of more basic problems with bugs, AI issues, and a widely-disliked UI. It remains stuck with a "mixed" user rating on Steam, and concurrent player numbers on the platform lag well behind not just Civilization 6, but the 15-year-old Civ 5 too... Read more.

notes.title: This Month in Civ: July Update, News Recap, and More
notes.notes:
[h1][b]Welcome Back![/b][/h1][p]Hey,[i] Civ [/i]fans! Welcome to This Month in [i]Civ[/i]! July has been a busy month, and we’re kicking things off with a recap of everything that’s happened so far. [/p][p]Let’s dive in![/p][p][/p][h1][b]July Update Notes[/b][/h1][h3][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXdcU3flkjFTOgxxSZJ-YLyDQEPWuyyiuiMqSQSzoL2mYEiEeFuJj77_kGQT18I6w2OOM1K6U9z5PuuBTS_yETZe_Vt47jBUll6iyeK495MARGJb0EL1KaK130hG1s7TWlnSBSHQ3g?key=VJokNal762ePcRr4h9mkt9U-"][/img][b]Update 1.2.3 is here![/b][/h3][p]This update introduces the first in a series of adjustments designed to enhance the Age Transition experience and soften the abruptness with a new game setting called “Continuity,” which is on by default. These changes affect Units, Unit placement, an End-of-Age turn timer, Independent Power spawns, and more, so check out the full notes for details! Outside of Age Transition changes, auto-explore makes its return, alongside changes to Advisor warnings, a new unique Commander Trung Nhi for the leader [url="https://civilization.2k.com/civ-vii/game-guide/leaders/trung-trac/"][u]Trung Trac[/u][/url] with a custom upgrade tree, and usual improvements to UI and various quality-of-life changes. Read the full details [url="https://civilization.2k.com/civ-vii/game-update-notes/"][u]here[/u][/url], or join QA Lead Shaun Wilson in our newest Developer Update Video as he dives into the details below.[/p][list][*][p]Auto-Explore [/p][/*][*][p]Updated Advisor Warnings [/p][/*][*][p]Age Transition Improvements ([i]Access the new “Continuity” setting after selecting your leader and civ in Advanced Options -> Game Settings -> Age Transition Impact[/i])[/p][/*][*][p]10 Turn End-of-Age Warning[/p][/*][*][p]Trung Nhi (Unique Commander for Trung Trac)[/p][/*][*][p]Challenges for DLC Leaders[/p][/*][/list][h3][b]Civilization VII Developer Update - July 2025[/b][/h3][previewyoutube="6BqH0oqlJLk;full"][/previewyoutube][p][/p][h1][b]Civ News[/b][/h1][h3][b]Civilization VII 4K Desktop Wallpapers[/b][/h3][p]If you're looking to change up your desktop background, here's a host of gorgeous historic scenes to choose from. We've heard that you love [i]Civilization VII[/i]'s art, so we've uploaded 4K versions of all the [i]Civ VII[/i] backgrounds [u][url="https://civilization.2k.com/civ-vii/media/"]here[/url][/u]. Go download something nice![/p][p][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXf1zU6CvjutUotuXhte5jXGzI_UDDW4vccjmYQ0zWK310vTJQvNQKsOalZz-dkRjLFZfW2DUHxz9aQ8YsO8po6Erg_TmgUcmS_dbCmSBY0vlG99v5QppXf7CrB9XRysxgYhXBAIFg?key=VJokNal762ePcRr4h9mkt9U-"][/img][/p][h3][b]
Right to Rule Content[/b][/h3][p]For those who own the [i]Founder’s Edition[/i], the first half of the Right to Rule Collection* is now available. This Collection includes a new leader, [url="https://civilization.2k.com/civ-vii/game-guide/leaders/genghis-khan/"][u]Genghis Khan[/u][/url],[b] [/b]check out his playstyle [url="https://youtu.be/0ULKVZkJj_M"][u]here[/u][/url], and two new civilizations, [url="https://civilization.2k.com/civ-vii/game-guide/civilizations/dai-viet/"][u]Dai Viet[/u][/url] and [url="https://civilization.2k.com/civ-vii/game-guide/civilizations/assyria/"][u]Assyria[/u][/url]. [/p][p][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXcfzEUnLicTdgRNljyDlSkuaIhiwTDMX60yQqbzQa8jNKksNfq69tjNzPu8kyTBcsglNkekGLXBiST6XIxp0vG6boZabM-mabii7QRbGRHAvl_Rmwpbv1PEJCeAGVF0DCCxjgKyjw?key=VJokNal762ePcRr4h9mkt9U-"][/img][/p][h3][b]Genghis Khan First Look[/b][/h3][previewyoutube="0ULKVZkJj_M;full"][/previewyoutube][h3][u][url="https://civilization.2k.com/civ-vii/game-guide/civilizations/dai-viet/"][b]Dai Viet Game Guide[/b][/url][/u][/h3][p][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXdAlQprp00L3VTwWWXpneDMrUNfjM_zq5ZSQ2AEiSF0HzIC_vEkzMWz5pYIAesnUivLJbqcA79X0afgnonjymo38dgi2DQuYkTkrHKON8uIsAHgrN3P3-isEXx4BAfvgPOqEdfw1w?key=VJokNal762ePcRr4h9mkt9U-"][/img][/p][h3][u][url="https://civilization.2k.com/civ-vii/game-guide/civilizations/assyria/"][b]Assyria Game Guide[/b][/url][/u][/h3][p][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXd0yx7YnJ9v2xbJYrVWceIS676l4uHv2hXv2ZrsIRG4NGr7zQ0OY_aoqv4-BG7InhrHHE7pRT_LbQMgD9k4qUB6VS6sNyif_5hwtg4dIVER9PjOTk_bryKH-PyWG_pHzWuD81TYnQ?key=VJokNal762ePcRr4h9mkt9U-"][/img][/p][p][i]*Right to Rule Collection is included in the Founders Edition of Civilization VII. It is also available for separate purchase (base game required). Each DLC will be delivered automatically in-game on release. Terms apply.[/i][/p][p][/p][h1][b]Developers Share Their Favorites[/b][/h1][p]You'll never find a shortage of passion at Firaxis. We asked the devs: “What was some of your favorite work in [i]Civilization VII[/i]?”[/p][p][/p][h3][b]Finn - Senior Narrative Designer[/b][/h3][p][i]“Bulgaria was a favorite of mine to work on. A persistent threat to Byzantium, the Bulgarian Empires had a rich militaristic, artistic, and spiritual history that still resounds today. It was a fun challenge to adapt their unique style and strengths to Civilization, and to highlight notable moments through Narrative Events in their first foray into the series.”[/i][/p][p][/p][h3][b]Rachel - Lead Animator[/b][/h3][p]“[i]My favorite leader that I have gotten to work on was Harriet Tubman. It was such an honor to get to animate on such an inspirational person. We also had an amazing voice actor who brought me to tears with her soulful singing and performance.[/i]”[/p][p][/p][h3][b]Dmytro - Sound Designer[/b][/h3][p]“[i]My favorite sound effect I created for Civilization VII must have been the Diplomacy Actions, especially the new ones for the Independent Powers. I really loved the idea of having fun sound effects happening when I embark on diplomacy, and making some sounds with some older flutes was a blast! It's also fun to just think about "What is the sound of befriending? Bolstering the military? Espionage?" and then try to make those sounds a reality[/i].”[/p][p][/p][h3][b]Daniella - Materials Artist[/b][/h3][p]“[i]My favorite civ to make materials for was hands-down the Shawnee set. I got to work directly with the Shawnee Tribe to pick out colors and patterns that would be culturally appropriate, and we were able to get a lot of very cool references from them. It was a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity and I’m very proud of the work that we did for that set.[/i] [/p][p][i]This was my favorite material that I made from that set; the Shawnee utilize a lot of quilting in their crafts, so we recreated some of their patterns, including the Squash Blossom.[/i]”[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45050851/067de6977c6ba72b722b518308ef6f1f85d45515.png"][/img][/p][h1][b]Community Highlights[/b][/h1][h3][b]Discord Screenshot Contest Winner[/b][/h3][p]Congrats to TheEpicMMX for winning “The Perfect Vacation” screenshot contest and claiming the title "Screenshot Champion."[/p][p][b]theepicmmx[/b][/p][p][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXfsjOTIi4SwmUZLvWa3JmGYDky4XAa4toNx2AliS4YQnsZyqklcp1ykz9NncUujlgHMv12BaYCiGuWm_TCHZFZGiQt3_Ka9cg2rHzNO4p4qnMV_fY28PNqTLEUmNdF8XhDwcGwM6A?key=VJokNal762ePcRr4h9mkt9U-"][/img][/p][h3][b]Honorable Contest Mentions[/b][/h3][p][b]ZZAlba [/b][/p][p][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXd6Kmh_L6F6UzLG8DMHAmyPzMrtvilrLXb5aTdSE7naU01RgcbMw3vrIZNIt8pHIsGfPtApSXoFOd4YgqytycvpJXKCIFiMRQsfbnj6R-YRhuSBrlY1AlFnF-bdLT2KPpnirWHr?key=VJokNal762ePcRr4h9mkt9U-"][/img][/p][p][b]The Oracle 
[/b][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXe89nN3cudmFtAsgWGT9mghG_alCsIpEhJ3U2pdYNP9ODlWRKF0hzvVRhCz5okw0F3WhG86VvCn3ziS_t1HB7JqtPGJA2SUfLTyWqGUQ8Oa7SGCPplw3wVy6zgXNMtjh3T-7sdTjg?key=VJokNal762ePcRr4h9mkt9U-"][/img][/p][p][b]Meache[/b][/p][p][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXfSn9L8ZYnWcscEcyV4jQQzLUlyq4-3MhCibySKDWvWfobs-NlYU-qIorQTAaPv6izmdeMrN3FNI2cdMaiyVcHfYpqiZBi9tLQ6THaJ9sGDwEKlmBKp6rgIH2Hozd2J_-VjWsdpIA?key=VJokNal762ePcRr4h9mkt9U-"][/img]Join us in the [url="https://discord.com/invite/civilizationofficial"][u]Official Discord[/u][/url] in #community-contests and check out the other submissions. Visit the channel to stay informed about future events, and for your chance to claim a contest title. Not interested in contests? Feel free to join the general chat or any of the other channels and hang with the community. See ya there![/p][p][/p][h3][b]We'll see you here next month![/b][/h3][p]News aside, thank you for all your feedback, both critical and kind. We know your passion for [i]Civilization [/i]drives your comments, and you want to see the best game possible. Please keep voicing your thoughts and contributing to a [i]Civilization[/i] you believe in.  If you haven't added your voice, start in our[url="https://discord.com/invite/civilizationofficial"] [u]Official Discord[/u][/url] and give feedback or chat with others about the updates. The Steam discussions are also a place to talk about feature requests, suggestions, guides, mods, and more. Stay connected with [i]Civ[/i] news delivered straight to your inbox. [url="https://civilization.2k.com/civ-vii/2k-account-benefits/#newsletter"][u]Sign up[/u][/url] for our newsletter now—your empire will thank you.[/p]

notes.title: Update 1.2.3 – Jul 22, 2025
notes.notes:
[p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45050851/68ef669c503e880ee7f95c686948bd75e6a5d502.png"][/img][/p][p]Hey [i]Civ[/i] fans,
[/p][p]Update 1.2.3 is rolling out now! This update is smaller in size, especially following the hefty list of changes from 1.2.2, but it still introduces some meaningful additions: the first round of improvements to Age Transitions, the return of auto-explore, several UI and quality-of-life updates, and a new Commander to join Trung Trac on the battlefield.[/p][p]If you caught our last [u][url="https://civilization.2k.com/civ-vii/news/civ-vii-update-check-in-jun-10/"]Dev Check-In[/url][/u], you know we're in the middle of some deeper work on systems like Ages, replayability, and how players connect with their civ across history. That work is underway, but it's going to take time. In the meantime, we're continuing to release updates like this one to smooth out rough edges and introduce long-requested features, while we keep pushing on the bigger things behind the scenes.[/p][p]This update also includes the first half of the new Content Collection, titled Right to Rule* – for many of you, this is part of what you already picked up with [i]Civilization VII's Founder's Edition[/i]. We'll have the full details below. [/p][p]And lastly, a few quick notes before you dive in:[/p][list][*][p]While we aim to maintain backwards compatibility for existing saves as much as possible, some new abilities or effects may not appear until you start a new game or advance to the next Age in your current campaign. For the best experience, we recommend starting a new game, or continuing your current game into the next Age.[/p][/*][*][p]If you encounter any new bugs or issues, try disabling any mods, as some may not yet be compatible with the latest update.[/p][/*][*][p]Are you playing on Steam and want to finish your current save under a previous version? You can do so using our legacy Steam beta branch.[/p][/*][/list][p]Thank you again to everyone sticking with us, sharing feedback, or just showing up to see what's new in the world of [i]Civ[/i]. Without further ado, here's what's in Update 1.2.3![/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45050851/cf1e15b95cd90e21bd97ff3353846210d28860f6.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p][b] [/b][/p][h1][b]Age Transition Improvements[/b][/h1][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45050851/ee681751a14194ee7326efeb3071255a25857a11.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]In our [u][url="https://civilization.2k.com/civ-vii/news/civ-vii-update-check-in-jun-10/"]June 10 Update Check-In[/url][/u], we had a section named "The Journey So Far, and What's Ahead." We mentioned there that we had heard feedback from significant segments of our community that we needed to do more work on the abruptness of Age Transitions, improve the overall game replayability (looking especially hard at Legacy Paths), and search for new avenues to allow players to identify more deeply with their empire and its path through history.[/p][p]Much of that work is ongoing, and though some of the larger changes we have planned will take time, we do have a first round of Age improvements going live with this update, many of which aim to tackle Age Transition abruptness. Here's what's included: [/p][list][*][p][b]New Continuity Option – [/b]You can now pick the type of Age Transition impact you want, with the new default option called Continuity, and the existing option called Regroup. Here's what you can expect from Continuity:[/p][list][*][p]Your Units will stay where they were in the previous Age, but are upgraded to their new version for that Age.[/p][/*][*][p]Units in other players' borders will be expelled in the same manner as if you lost open borders, but will remain nearby.[/p][/*][*][p]In addition to what was carried over before, you now can transition with Ships and Siege Units from Antiquity to Exploration, as well as Settlers, Migrants, Scouts, and Merchants in all Ages.[/p][/*][*][p]You will no longer get Advisor Warnings for large armies.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Please note:[/b] pre-1.2.3 saves will still use the existing Age transition impact, Regroup.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p][b]Improved Relationship Management – [/b]Instead of sudden shifts to your relationships with other players after Age Transition, your relationships will now slowly be pulled back towards 0 over the course of the game. The further you are away from 0, the faster your relationship will decay. This should feel like a much more natural change to your relationships over time, and encourage you to push some Endeavors here and there to maintain your positive relationships, too. [/p][/*][*][p][b]End of Age Warnings – [/b]We've added a 10- (or more) turn safe zone at the end of each Age that guarantees you can finish your most critical tasks before the transition occurs. This countdown can be extended to 20 turns or turned off completely. No Age progression from any source other than elapsed turns will be added while the countdown is active.[/p][/*][/list][p]And, some other changes worth noting here: [/p][list][*][p]Catapults are now available at the start of the Exploration Age.[/p][/*][*][p]Merchants are now available at the start of the Exploration and Modern Ages.[/p][/*][*][p]Independent Powers will now spawn at the beginning of the Age, after an Age transition.[/p][/*][/list][p]We'll continue to expand Continuity mode in the future and are already working on other key areas of feedback, including replayability and player identity. Some of the bigger changes will take time, but we hope these updates help your next empire flow more smoothly between Ages. As always, let us know how it feels![/p][p][/p][h1][b]Auto-Explore[/b][/h1][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45050851/727284892c85363245c2ed2610d91b06aa14a347.jpg"][/img][/p][p]It's time: release the Scouts! [/p][p]We've mentioned before that Scout Units work a bit differently in [i]Civ VII [/i]than [i]Civ VI[/i], which is why we wanted players to have the opportunity to play with the Scout's new abilities, instead of adding in auto-explore right away. BUT – we hear you. Sometimes, it's easier to let the Scouts (and Ships) loose and allow them to find a Discovery, encounter a new civ, or even walk straight into danger. [/p][p]Here are all the Units that have access to auto-explore: [/p][list][*][p][b]All Ages[/b]: Scout + Unique Variants.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Exploration[/b]: Tier 2 and Tier 3 Naval Units (excluding the Cog, which we didn't want to sink from Ocean damage pre-Shipbuilding). [/p][/*][*][p][b]Modern[/b]: All Naval Units except the Submarine.[/p][/*][/list][p]Here's some auto-explore behavior you should keep in mind: Units will seek to maximize revealed tiles on a move. If they can't reveal any tiles within a single move, they'll try to explore unexplored areas closest to one of your existing Settlements. The Unit will also stop auto-exploring if there is a Discovery within two turns of movement range, or if they move into the Zone of Control of an enemy Unit.[/p][p]This is just the first implementation of this feature, and as we learned from our Discord feedback event, we have plenty more ideas in mind to expand things down the road. We look forward to making it better over time based on player feedback![/p][p][/p][h1][b]New Unique Commander: Trung Nhi[/b][/h1][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45050851/206b0765a90ca7565f160984c109168aae7b68ff.jpg"][/img][/p][p]Our designers have long wanted to give the leader [u][url="https://civilization.2k.com/civ-vii/game-guide/leaders/trung-trac/"]Trung Trac[/url][/u] a unique Army Commander to represent her legendary sisterhood, and with this update, Trung Nhi joins the battlefield![/p][p]Trung Nhi features a unique model, a custom Promotion Tree, and full gameplay functionality. She is granted automatically in the first Age, alongside the first Military Unit produced by a Trung Trac player (including Advanced Starts), and she persists across Ages. As part of this change, Trung Trac no longer grants three free Promotions to her first Commander. She also has a Unique Commendation, "Sisters Unite," which replaces Duty and adds +30 to Heroic Assault.[/p][p][b]Please note[/b]: pre-1.2.3 saves will not receive Trung Nhi! [/p][p][/p][p][b]Trung Nhi's Promotion Tree (replaces Leadership):[/b][/p][list][*][p]Jungle Warfare: +5 Combat Strength for Units in Tropical terrain within the Command Radius[/p][/*][*][p]Mettle and Courage: +5 Combat Strength for Units in friendly territory within the Command Radius[/p][/*][*][p]Lạc Rebellion: +3 Combat Strength for land Units in the Command Radius when Trung Nhi is adjacent to at least 2 enemies[/p][/*][*][p]One Single Cry: +5 Combat Strength with Coordinated Attack and Focus Fire[/p][/*][*][p]65 Strongholds: +5 Combat Strength against Fortified Districts within the Command Radius[/p][/*][*][p]Hai Bà Trưng: +15 Combat Strength for this Commander when defending[/p][/*][/list][p]Try out Trung Nhi by picking Trung Trac as your playable leader! For extra historical flavor for those with the paid content of Right to Rule Collection*, try pairing the Trung sisters with the release of Dai Viet as a DLC civ! [/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45050851/cf1e15b95cd90e21bd97ff3353846210d28860f6.png"][/img][/p][h1][b]New Features[/b][/h1][p][/p][h2]End of Age Countdown[/h2][list][*][p](★ – Community Influenced Item) An end of Age countdown option has been added to the Advanced Start options. The default is 10 turns, but it can be extended to 20 turns or turned off. No Age progression from any source other than elapsed turns will be added while the countdown is active.[/p][list][*][p][b]Dev Note: [/b]We know it was frustrating for some players when it felt like the end of an Age snuck up on you. We have even more improvements planned for Age Transitions down the line, so let us know how these changes feel![/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][h2]Trung Nhi (Unique Army Commander for Trung Trac)[/h2][list][*][p]Trung Nhi joins the battlefield as a new Commander Unit for Trung Trac, with a unique model and unique Promotion Tree that replaces Leadership (please note: pre-1.2.3 saves will not receive Trung Nhi!). The unique Promotion Tree includes: [/p][list][*][p][b]Jungle Warfare[/b]: +5 Combat Strength for Units in Tropical in the Command Radius.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Mettle and Courage[/b]: +5 Combat Strength for Units in the Command Radius when in friendly territory.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Lạc Rebellion[/b]: +2 Combat Strength for Land Units in the Command Radius when there are at least 2 adjacent enemies to Trung Nhi.[/p][/*][*][p][b]One Single Cry[/b]: +5 Combat Strength with Coordinated Attack and Focus Fire.[/p][/*][*][p][b]65 Strongholds[/b]: +5 Combat Strength against Fortified Districts for Units in the Command Radius.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Hai Bà Trung[/b]: +15 Combat Strength for this Commander when defending.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Trung Trac no longer awards 3 free Promotions for her first Commander. This is replaced with Trung Nhi being awarded in the first Age of every game played alongside the first Military Unit produced by the Trung Trac player (Note: Advanced Starts award her as well). [/p][/*][*][p]Trung Nhi, her abilities, promotions, and appearance persist across subsequent Ages.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][h1][b]Gameplay[/b][/h1][p][/p][p][b]Advisors[/b][/p][list][*][p](★) Made several improvements to Advisor Warnings, including:[/p][list][*][p]"Suffering War Weariness" no longer triggers when your opponent is suffering War Weariness.[/p][/*][*][p]"Nuclear Weapon Available" will no longer appear when the player has a WMD and a Bomber already built.[/p][/*][*][p]Several warnings no longer occur if you are more than 75% of the way through an Age, including "Surplus Influence," "Over Settlement Cap," and "Overflowing Treasury."
[/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][p][b]Age Transitions[/b][/p][list][*][p](★) Added a new Advanced setting allowing players to select their preferred method of Age Transitions: Continuity or Regroup. [/p][/*][*][p](★) Catapults are now available at the start of the Exploration Age.[/p][/*][*][p](★) Merchants are now available at the start of the Exploration and Modern Ages.[/p][/*][*][p](★) Independent Powers will now spawn at the beginning of the Age, after an Age Transition.[/p][/*][*][p]Legacy Points will now correctly spend when the player changes deck from Custom to Preset in the Advanced Menu.[/p][/*][*][p]Staatseisenbahn can no longer appear on road tiles when a roundabout or crossroad is created during the Advanced Start phase when playing as any civ but Prussia.
[/p][/*][/list][p][b]Diplomacy[/b][/p][list][*][p]The effect of Preservation Societies Social Policy can no longer be stacked by repeatedly slotting it in and out of the player's Government.[/p][/*][*][p]Improved relationship management with other leaders, so that relationships will now slowly be pulled back towards 0 over the course of the game, instead of sudden shifts at Age transition. Every five turns your relationship with other players will shift back to neutral by a small amount, and this amount is greater the further your relationship is from neutral. [/p][list][*][p][b]Dev Note:[/b] The shift is stronger on the hostile side than the friendly side as there are more ways to hurt a relationship than improve it, and we didn't want to unduly punish players who want to pursue good relationships with their neighbors.[/p][p][/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][p][b]Environment[/b][/p][list][*][p]Ocean Resources are no longer highlighted when using America's Prospector Unique Civilian Unit.[/p][/*][/list][p]
[b]Economy[/b][/p][list][*][p]Lo'i Kalo adjacency bonus is now +1 Culture from adjacent Farms.[/p][/*][*][p](★) Buildings now retain their full base Yields and Maintenance costs on Age Transition. They will still lose adjacencies and special effects.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p][b]Legends & Mementos[/b][/p][list][*][p](★) Leaders from Crossroads of the World and Right to Rule DLC now have their full Legends challenges.[/p][/*][*][p](★) Added new challenges for Right to Rule DLC civs Dai Viet and Assyria.
[/p][/*][/list][p][b]Miscellaneous[/b][/p][list][*][p]The maximum number of players in a single-player game has been increased to 12 players for Huge maps, via the Advanced Options menu. Platforms that support Huge map sizes include PC, Mac, Linux, PS5, Xbox Series, and Nintendo Switch 2**.[/p][/*][*][p]Future Tech/Civics no longer grant Wildcard attribute points, and now give a random attribute point instead.[/p][list][*][p][b]Dev Note[/b]: These repeatable rewards were causing the overall impact of the attribute system to be greater than intended and started to overshadow your unique leader and civ abilities.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p](★) Maya's Jaguar Slayer and Inca's Chasqui Unique Scout Units now have the "Pet the Dog" ability.[/p][/*][*][p]Heroic Assault Commander ability can no longer target Civilian Units when a Civilian Unit is in the Command Radius during gameplay.[/p][/*][*][p]Commander Attack (Duty ability | Heroic Assault) is no longer able to target enemy Units inside a Walled tile when performing the ability.[/p][/*][*][p]Added Advanced Option Setting for AI Settlements receiving free Walls when they complete the Age-specific Wall Tech.[/p][/*][*][p]Recommended civs now properly appear as Age Unlocks when viewing the leaders in the Choose Leader menu.[/p][/*][*][p]The Delete button is no longer missing when attempting to delete the Sepoy Unique Infantry Unit.[/p][/*][*][p]Addressed a reported issue where the incorrect number of AI players would be displayed when hosting a multiplayer lobby on a Small/Tiny map.
[/p][/*][/list][h1][b]UI[/b][/h1][p][b]General[/b][/p][list][*][p](★) The total amount of Yield needed for researching or producing items is now visible to the player.[/p][/*][*][p]The Policy screen now remembers the last screen viewed.[/p][/*][*][p]Turns remaining for Quests now show next to the title for cleaner visibility.[/p][/*][*][p]The Age Progress tab now remembers which Legacy Path tab the player was on when it was closed.[/p][/*][*][p]Proper items now display in the Production menu of a Town with Fort Town Specialization.[/p][/*][*][p]Confucius' portrait no longer appears when viewing the Leader Targets of the "Independent – Incite Raid" Project of any hostile Independent Power.[/p][/*][*][p]The Enter key on the keyboard now functions properly when triggering the Lens Toggles menu.[/p][/*][*][p]Research queue is now cancelled when the player selects any Civic or Tech available for research.[/p][/*][*][p]Redundant Confirm Quitting message no longer appears shortly when clicking close icon twice during Windowed screen mode.[/p][/*][*][p]Slots of Commanders are no longer missing when the player checks the spawn Commander after selecting Militaristic Dark Age.[/p][/*][*][p]Hotkeys/keybindings now function properly when the player has a Unit selected on the Map.[/p][/*][*][p]The Swap button will no longer be missing when the player tries to use a mouse to swap or choose a Unit in the Unit panel.

many [i]Founder's Edition[/i] owners have been waiting for: the first part of the paid Right to Rule DLC*, introducing the new leader Genghis Khan, two new civs Assyria and Dai Viet, and four new Wonders! The second and final part of Right to Rule, currently targeting September 2025, will include the leader Lakshmibai and the civs Silla and Qajar. [/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45050851/03f79d8c2060e756673fd46c821ab88c6aba2081.jpg"][/img][/p][h2]Leaders[/h2][p][/p][p][b](Right to Rule DLC*) Added new leader Genghis Khan.[/b][/p][p]Born Temüjin, Genghis Khan accomplished a seemingly impossible feat for a man with humble origins – to unite the nomadic Mongol tribes under his singular leadership. His ambitions did not stop with the Mongols, however, and he embarked on campaigns that brought under his control northern China and the eastern portion of the Silk Road. The nature of Genghis Khan's death remains a mystery, unlike his inimical accomplishments.[/p][list][*][p][b]Attributes:[/b] Expansionist, Militaristic[/p][/*][*][p][b]Unique Ability - Chosen of Tengri[/b]: +3 Combat Strength to Cavalry units this becomes +5 when in an Army Command Radius. Army Commanders have full movement with zero packed units. Decrease Relationship by a Small Amount for the leader with the most amount of Cavalry units in an empire.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45050851/296d9e20b13525cf823114f15ed38b80333ce26a.jpg"][/img][/p][/*][/list][h2]Civilizations[/h2][p][/p][p][b](Right to Rule DLC*) Added a new Antiquity Age civilization Assyria.[/b][/p][p]Nestled in the Fertile Crescent, Assyria was one of the earliest states to dominate the region. From beginnings in the city of Ashur to the rise of the great Neo-Assyrian Empire, a long succession of kings would oversee the bloody conquest of Babylon, Egypt, and others – acting as a conduit for Mesopotamian culture throughout the lands. These conquests would later spell doom for Assyria, as a Babylonian revolt ended the empire in 609 BCE.[/p][list][*][p][b]Attributes[/b]: Military, Science[/p][/*][*][p][b]Unique Ability - Treasures of Nineveh:[/b] Gain a Technology upon capturing a Settlement for the first time. [/p][/*][/list][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45050851/b8de1626b2fa54597b67dd0da5e9230e67042c4f.png"][/img][/p][p][b](Right to Rule DLC*)] Added a new Exploration Age civilization Dai Viet.[/b][/p][p]Vietnamese history is a dance of resistance and expansion. The medieval Đại Việt kingdom, especially under the Trần Dynasty, stood against Mongol invasions, even as it expanded southward into Cham lands. This dialectic of resistance and conquest led to the creation of a unique Vietnamese culture, one influenced but not dominated by Chinese sources, and a strong sense of identity.[/p][list][*][p][b]Attributes[/b]: Expansionist, Cultural[/p][/*][*][p][b]Unique Ability - Hịch Tướng Sĩ:[/b] When you create a Fortification Constructible receive 5 Culture for every urban population in that Settlement. (Scales By Game Speed)[/p][/*][*][p][b]Unique Civilian Unit[/b]: Quận Vương (Unique Settler Unit)[/p][/*][*][p][b]Unique Military Unit[/b]: Voi Chiến (Unique Ranged Unit)[/p][/*][*][p][b]Associated Wonder[/b]: Thanh Hue[/p][/*][/list][h2]Wonders[/h2][p][b](Right to Rule DLC*) Added four new Wonders: [/b][/p][list][*][p][b]Mausoleum at Halicarnassus[/b] – Antiquity[/p][/*][*][p][b]Wat Xieng Thong[/b] – Exploration[/p][/*][*][p][b]Grand Bazaar[/b] – Exploration[/p][/*][*][p][b]Ubudiah Mosque[/b] – Modern [/p][/*][/list][p][i]**Right to Rule Collection is included in the Founders Edition of Civilization VII. It is also available for separate purchase (base game required). Terms apply.[/i]
[/p][p][i]**The Nintendo Switch version of the game only supports the Tiny, and Small map sizes; it does not support map sizes of Standard and above. For cross-play multiplayer games with players on Nintendo Switch, these map size restrictions will apply.[/i][/p]

notes.title: Civ VII Developer Update - July 2025 | Highlights for tomorrow's 1.2.3 update!
notes.notes: [h2][b]Update 1.2.3 is landing tomorrow![/b][/h2][p][/p][p]Including Auto-Explore, Age Transition Improvements, and a new unique Commander, Trung Nhi! Hear more about it from the dev team here: [/p][previewyoutube="6BqH0oqlJLk;full"][/previewyoutube][p][/p][p]Also coming alongside tomorrow's update for all our [i]Founder's Edition[/i] owners: the first part of Right to Rule*! Genghis Khan, alongside Dai Viet and Assyria, will be releasing with 1.2.3. notes.title: New Civ 7 update improves a controversial mechanic and brings back a classic one
notes.notes:
It's been five months since Civilization 7 launched, and it's still struggling to find its feet. Civ 6 is pulling in loads more players on Steam, and recent user reviews for the sequel sit at 'mostly negative.' Issues like a lacking UI, the controversial Ages system, and missing key features are all weighing the game down. But that doesn't mean Firaxis isn't putting the work in. The studio has been consistently updating Civ 7 since launch, gradually improving the experience and acting on player feedback. Now, with update 1.2.3 around the corner, Firaxis is taking another look at Ages and finally bringing a key feature back.

Read the rest of the story...

notes.title: Civilization 7 is getting auto-explore for scouts, reminding me that I both hate and love auto-explore
notes.notes:
The next major Sid Meier's Civilization VII update will make some fairly sizeable tweaks to Firaxis' latest, not-greatest 4X strategy sim. It'll rearrange the workings of age transitions, with a view to providing a bit more continuity between epochs and helping you finish your to-do list before crossing the threshold. We can expect a new commander, too - Trưng Nhị, sister to existing Vietnamese leader Trưng Trắc.

Perhaps most significantly, the feature will re-introduce auto-explore mechanics for scouts. This piques my interest, inasmuch as I haven't ever thought critically about auto-explore mechanics, and now that I do, I realise I regard them with a mixture of enthusiasm and spite.

Read more

Big fixes are in the works, however, and the most recent update feels like the start of a climb in the right direction. But there are some problems that can be more immediately fixed, and modders have done exactly that with the introduction of a tool to easily see exactly the effect of new policies.

notes.title: Mighty Civilization 7 update adds Huge maps, but beware, your PC might struggle to run them
notes.notes:
Sid Meier's Civilization VII has received another big update, as the rather divisive 4X strategy game wrangles with a mostly negative user review consensus on Steam.

The latest Civ 7 update adds large and huge maps, each with a default of 10 players in single player and eight (including AI) in multiplayer. Developers Firaxis are working on supporting 12 players for Huge maps, but need more time to ensure that this doesn't scuttle game stability and performance. As it is, they caution that "bigger maps have bigger hardware demands" and that you might see "slower turn times or performance drops, especially on lower end hardware."

Read more

notes.title: New Civilization 7 update makes huge changes to Ages mechanic, adds sandbox mode
notes.notes:
Here I am again to argue that Civilization 7, as much as it may be too radical a departure from 4X game tradition, has the potential to be very, very good. Four months since Firaxis launched the strategy sequel and its Steam user ratings are still relatively dismal. Players find that the Ages system fractures and breaks the flow of your empire building, and that certain mechanics like crises and Legacy paths are too punitive or limiting. Competition is stiff. Stellaris keeps evolving, Ara History Untold is mounting a comeback, and beloved classics like Age of Empires 2 and even Civ 5 and 6 are pulling players away from Firaxis' latest. The new Civilization 7 update, however, feels like it could mark the beginning of a turnaround.

Read the rest of the story...
